children: DraftKings says it will get returns on costs to acquire prediction-markets customers before the expected Supreme Court ruling on predictions in mid-2028. For spending to acquire customers in 2026, the company expects paybacks within about 20 months, Chief Executive Jason Robins tells analysts on a call. Robins expects a similar timeline for investments made in 2027, with faster paybacks if the Supreme Court approves sports predictions to continue. Even if the markets are banned by July 2028, DraftKings expects returns on its 2027 customer acquisition costs in four years or less, Robins says. That is because the company is betting it can sell customers on non-sports predictions and other products it offers, he says.(katherine.hamilton@wsj.com)
